Keeping the attempt entry is what stops a further push on the redelivery a lost ACK brings, inside attemptCacheTTL. The deployed CloudWatch filter on `listener exception publish failed` (infra/aws/rendering/metricfilters.go:65) still matches, so the operator signal survives the removal of the retry. TestAGiveUpWhoseNoticeCanNeverBePublishedIsStillTerminal pins it.

internal/bus/confirm.go:30-33 and nats.go:902-904 (5dfa3c9746f7): no message is emitted once its context has ended, by two checks that see different things. publishConfirmed refuses a deadline already spent immediately before it publishes, closing the class for every caller of it; publishCoreTo refuses a ctx whose Err is set, which catches a cancellation whose deadline is still ahead and which publishConfirmed cannot see, since it is given a deadline and not a context. errWindowElapsed keeps the previous error text so a deployed filter still matches. keyFindings.description: Two required checks are red at the code head 3175373656f8: typecheck (job 121147417642) and test (job 121147417424). Both fail on one Go compile error, and it is in the merge GitHub builds for a pull_request event rather than in this branch's own tree: 'packages/envoy/internal/testnats/nats.go:25:2: rand redeclared in this block', '"math/rand/v2" imported as rand and not used', ':535:61: undefined: rand.IntN'. main now imports math/rand/v2 as rand in that file and calls rand.IntN (read at refs/heads/main, line 505); this branch adds crypto/rand to the same import block for accountSecret. Git merges both import lines without reporting a conflict, and Go then refuses the package: rand is declared twice, the branch's rand.Read binds crypto/rand, and main's rand.IntN no longer resolves. The branch's own tree compiles, which is why nothing before this read caught it - the tester cited Tests as in progress and did not wait. This is a semantic conflict with the base, so bringing main forward is justified under the conflict rule rather than being an unprompted base merge; the import needs an alias on one side. Never approve a head whose code is red.

This round made publishNoHolderExceptionOrNak dead and kept it. Its only remaining caller is fanoutDelivery (delivery.go:917), and listenerDeliveryHandler routes every role topic to roleTopicDelivery and every agent topic to agentSubjectDelivery (delivery.go:293-300), so a topic reaching fanoutDelivery is never a control topic and the function's first statement returns true before anything is published. The publish, the exceptionPublishFailedLine log, the messagesNAKed increment and the finalize(true) NAK in its body are now unreachable, as is the `if !...{ return }` at the call site. The function's own doc comment states this, so the deadness is deliberate rather than overlooked. Code made obsolete by a cutover is in scope for the change that obsoletes it: delete the helper and reduce the call site to its logger.Info line. The code-quality pass raised the same thing. Not a behaviour defect; raised because an unreachable NAK path in the one file whose retry policy this issue rewrote is exactly what a later reader will reason from.

publishCoreTo checks ctx.Err() before ensureConnWithContext, which can then wait for a reconnect; a cancellation arriving during that wait is not seen again, because publishConfirmed is given a deadline rather than a context and the deadline may still be ahead. The window is the reconnect wait, and the consequence is the one this round just closed at a different instant: a core publish emitted for a caller that has gone. Raised by the code-quality pass, verified in the code, and not blocking - the two checks close the reachable cases and this one needs the caller to cancel inside the wait.

The terminal give-up's no-second-push property rests on the attempt-cache entry, which is process memory with a five-minute TTL (attemptCacheTTL, main.go). A lost ACK whose redelivery arrives after a restart, or after the TTL, finds no entry and pushes again. The architect already scoped this and the give-up's own comment names attemptCacheTTL; the durable's AckWait is 60 s, so the redelivery a lost ACK brings is well inside the TTL for a live process. Recorded, not blocking.
